strengths: Novel application of loss vector embeddings for client clustering with clear practical advantages over IFCA (no careful initialization needed) and CFL-S (convergence in 2-3 rounds vs. hundreds)
Applicable to both supervised and unsupervised settings, which is rare for CFL methods and demonstrated on autoencoders
Comprehensive experimental evaluation covering multiple datasets, extensive heterogeneity scenarios (label skew, feature skew, concept shift), up to 1000 clients, and ablation studies
Strong empirical results: consistently achieves near-perfect clustering (ARI ≈ 1.0) in 2-3 rounds with competitive or superior model accuracy across all tasks
Solid theoretical contributions for linear regression (Theorems 4.1-4.2) with detailed proofs connecting loss vector separation to proximity conditions
Robustness to initialization clearly demonstrated (Figure 2), addressing a major practical limitation of IFCA
Practical features including early stopping once clusters stabilize and simple, implementable algorithm
Extensive supplementary material with detailed experimental setup, code availability promised, and reproducible hyperparameters
weaknesses: Theory restricted to linear regression with strong assumptions (orthonormal initialization, unit-norm optimal models, Δ≈1, σ≪1); significant gap between theory and practice on complex tasks like CIFAR-10 CNNs
Core technical contribution relatively incremental—standard k-means clustering on loss vectors; clustering algorithm and initialization strategy not fully specified, limiting reproducibility
Communication overhead from broadcasting K models until stabilization not formally analyzed; claimed mitigation (weight-sharing layers) not empirically evaluated
When K unknown, Algorithm 2 requires clustering for multiple K values and computing silhouette scores, but computational cost and robustness of K selection not analyzed (only Table 12)

Limited failure mode analysis: no deep investigation of performance degradation when clusters have similar distributions or when K is misspecified; Figure 3(a) shows degrading performance with small Δ but lacks analysis

Privacy treatment superficial: Section C.2 acknowledges loss vectors' privacy implications are 'underexplored' while claiming they're 'not privacy-sensitive' (contradictory); no formal privacy guarantees
Some baseline methods perform surprisingly poorly (FeSEM: 11.2% on CIFAR-10; CFL-S: 82.5±21.8 on MNIST) raising concerns about proper tuning; high variance in some IFCA results (85.7±6.5) unexplained
Experimental design choices not justified: Why T=100 rounds? Why τ=1 local epoch? Stability criterion (3 consecutive rounds) seems arbitrary with no sensitivity analysis
Limited ablation studies: k-means vs FINCH comparison (Table 18) provided, but k-means initialization strategy, other clustering algorithms, and bipartite matching robustness not explored
Incomplete baseline comparisons: Recent work (Licciardi et al. 2025, Vardhan et al. 2024) dismissed without direct empirical comparison; unclear if all methods hyperparameter-tuned equally
